geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the generic bar with a split-wing mass to introduce a real void and stronger hierarchy at the ground plane.
Keep the mass aligned longitudinally across the site.
Open a larger public gap so the access edge becomes a meaningful threshold.
Maintain one connected dominant building body after the split.
Turn the existing carve toward the verified access side to strengthen the street-facing public threshold.
Enlarge the carve slightly so it reads as usable public ground instead of a minor cut.

graph_edits.rationale: Reframe the primary mass as a split-wing composition to create a clearer dominant bar with an integrated public threshold instead of a sealed single extrusion.
Keep the main gesture longitudinal while allowing a clearer ground-level separation on the frontage side.
Introduce a readable void ratio strong enough to register as public space rather than a decorative notch.
Lower and calm the upper mass so the street edge reads as capacity-aware housing/commercial fabric rather than an overemphatic sculptural top.
Preserve connectivity across the split so the form remains one coherent building rather than two unrelated pieces.
Align the public void to the verified access side in the program frame so the ground response is legible at the street edge.

rationale: The candidate is coherent across views as a single compact mass, so it avoids obvious fragmentation and repairs reasonably well within the parcel. However, the dominant gesture reads as a mostly boxy bar with a small top extrusion rather than a clearly authored neighborhood-building figure. The verified access edge is not convincingly answered: the visible road edge gets only a small incision/void and no strong public threshold, while the mass remains semantically more sealed than opened. The stepped upper profile is present but not compelling as inhabited section; it feels more like an incidental roof modulation than a program-supporting terrace or daylight structure. Compared with the references, it borrows some bar-and-void vocabulary but lacks the legible courtyard/public-ground logic of the similar precedents and does not yet support the active-ground neighborhood brief. As a result, program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The campus/office scale is larger and more complex than this neighborhood-living candidate; use the void-and-bridge relationship, not the overall complexity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking bar volumes with a substantial central void/courtyard and clear support hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a more pavilion-like retail/hospitality object; it is useful for ground response but not for the candidate’s current stepped/bridge-like section.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple low-rise street-facing massing with a clear entry threshold and a compact service-like vertical accent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate only weakly achieves the inhabited-terrain effect; its section reads more like a clipped stacked bar than an integrated terrace section.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced roof/massing can be legitimate when it is tied to usable edge condition, courtyard logic, and continuous habitation.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied from the provided diagram, but the access-edge response is weak.
Open-space figure is too small and under-semanticized to count as a meaningful public void.
The silhouette is coherent, but the section does not yet communicate a convincing neighborhood-living hierarchy.
Do not overcorrect into a tower or large-span typology; the brief wants an active low/mid-rise street building.
